Name: TrueWindow
Author: kaniclub
Description:
[center][size=6][b][i]TrueWindow[/i][/b][/size][/center]
[center][i]Add real-time outdoor views to TrueWindow-enabled furniture.[/i][/center]

[center][size=4][url=https://ibb.co/fYkr5gwg][img]https://i.ibb.co/0jCYS7b7/b-simple-9-2-L.png[/img][/url][/size][/center]

[b]TrueWindow is [u]not[/u] a mod that adds new windows by itself.[/b]

It is a feature mod that lets compatible furniture display outdoor scenery inside the glass area.

When you place TrueWindow-enabled furniture indoors, the glass part can show a [b]real-time outdoor view[/b], making it feel like you are actually looking outside.

This means TrueWindow is designed to work together with mods or Content Patcher packs that add [b]TrueWindow-compatible furniture[/b].

[center]

[img]https://i.ibb.co/gZTXDm8H/image.gif[/img][/center]
[b][size=5]Features[/size][/b]

[list]
[*]Displays real-time outdoor scenery inside the glass area of compatible furniture[/*]
[*]Makes indoor spaces feel like they have actual windows to the outside[/*]
[*]Lets you adjust the view per location through the furniture settings[/*]
[*]Supports multiple display sources[/*]
[*]Real-time location view[/*]
[*]Built-in Mountain image[/*]
[*]Built-in Ocean image[/*]
[*]Built-in Night Sky image[/*]
[*]A custom image defined by a Content Pack[/*]
[*]Lets furniture authors define reserved colors, default view settings, whether right-click config is allowed, and whether furniture glow effects should be rendered[/*]
[/list][center][/center]

[size=5][b]Built-in Image Presets[/b][/size]

TrueWindow also includes built-in image presets that can be selected as a display source.

You can also set your own custom image through a Content Pack by using SpecifiedImage[.

[size=4][b]Custom Images from Compatible Mods[/b][/size]

Compatible mods can register custom images through the TrueWindow API, available since version 1.0.6. Registered images can be selected as a display source in the furniture settings.

For instructions on adding images, refer to the documentation of the mod providing them.

[size=5][b]Important Notes[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]TrueWindow is a [b]feature/framework-style mod[/b], not a furniture pack by itself[/*]
[*]At the moment, TrueWindow supports [b]furniture only[/b][/*]
[*]It does [b]not[/b] currently support buildings, walls, wallpaper, or direct map tile replacement[/*]
[*]To add your own compatible windows, you will usually pair TrueWindow with [b]Content Patcher furniture edits/additions[/b][/*]
[/list][center][/center]

[b][size=6]Settings[/size]
[/b]

TrueWindow has two kinds of settings: [b]main mod settings [/b]and [b]furniture display settings[/b].

[size=4][b]Main Settings
[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]RenderThrottleFrames[/b]
Minimum number of frames between redraws. Higher values reduce redraw frequency and can improve performance.[/*]
[*][b]IndoorProbeIntervalTicks[/b]
How often the mod checks again when no TrueWindow furniture is found in the current indoor area.[/*]
[*][b]MaxRenderScale[/b]
Internal upper limit for render scaling.[/*]
[*][b]MinEditableZoom[/b]
Minimum zoom value allowed in the furniture display settings.[/*]
[*][b]MaxEditableZoom[/b]
Maximum zoom value allowed in the furniture display settings.[/*]
[/list]

[size=4][b]Furniture Display Settings

[img]https://i.ibb.co/C52Tt0SF/settings.png[/img]
[/b][/size]

Right-clicking TrueWindow-enabled furniture lets you change display settings for the current location.
These settings are saved in the save data.

[list]
[*][b][size=3]DisplaySource[/size][/b]
[size=3]Choose what the furniture displays.[/size][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b][size=3]OffsetX[/size][/b]
[size=3]Horizontal display offset.[/size][/*]
[*][b][size=3]OffsetY[/size][/b]
[size=3]Vertical display offset.[/size][/*]
[*][b][size=3]Zoom[/size][/b]
[size=3]Zoom level for the outdoor view or image.[/size][/*]
[*][b][size=3]ParallaxStrength[/size][/b]
[size=3]Controls how strongly the view shifts based on player position.[/size][/*]
[/list][center][/center]

[size=5][b]For Mod Authors / Content Pack Authors[/b][/size]

If you want to make furniture compatible with TrueWindow, the basic idea is simple:

[list]
[*]The furniture must be identifiable as a TrueWindow target[/*]
[*]The part of the furniture texture that should display the view must be painted with a reserved color[/*]
[/list]

TrueWindow checks furniture [b]context tags[/b] to determine whether the furniture is compatible.

[size=4][b]Required tag[/b][/size]
truewindow

[size=4][b]Optional tag[/b][/size]
truewindow_id:your_id_here

If truewindow_id is present, TrueWindow uses that ID to look up the matching definition.
If it is not present, the furniture's ItemId is used instead.


[size=5][b]How the Glass Area Works[/b][/size]

The part of the furniture texture that should behave like glass must be painted with a [b]reserved color[/b].

The default reserved color is #FF00FF.

Only pixels painted with that color will be treated as the display area.
Be careful not to paint the frame or decorative trim with the reserved color unless you want those parts replaced too.


[size=5][b]Minimal Setup[/b][/size]

The smallest possible setup is:

[list]
[*]Add the truewindow tag to the furniture[/*]
[*]Paint the glass area with #FF00FF[/*]
[*]No truewindow.json is required[/*]
[*]No custom ID is required[/*]
[/list]

Example folder structure:

[code]﻿[CP] YourName.MinimalTrueWindow/
├─ manifest.json
├─ content.json
└─ assets/
└─ minimal_window.png[/code]
[center][/center]

[size=5][b]Full Setup[/b][/size]

If you want more control, you can use truewindow_id together with truewindow.json.

With the full setup, you can define things like:

[list]
[*]A specific TrueWindow definition ID[/*]
[*]A custom reserved color[/*]
[*]A default custom image[/*]
[*]Default offsets[/*]
[*]Default zoom[/*]
[*]Parallax strength[/*]
[*]Whether furniture glow effects are rendered[/*]
[*]Whether right-click configuration is allowed[/*]
[/list]

Example folder structure:

[code][CP] YourName.FullTrueWindow/
├─ manifest.json
├─ content.json
├─ truewindow.json
└─ assets/
├─ full_window.png
└─ mountain_view.png[/code]

Example SpecifiedImage setting:

[code]"SpecifiedImage": "assets/mountain_view.png"[/code]

You can place the image in the Content Pack root or inside assets, but using a clear relative path such as assets/filename.png is recommended.


[size=5][b]Definition File Locations[/b][/size]

TrueWindow can read definitions from any of the following places:

[list]
[*]content.json using a TrueWindow section[/*]
[*]truewindow.json[/*]
[*]assets/truewindow.json[/*]
[/list][center][/center]

[size=5][b]Definition Fields[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]TrueWindowId[/b]
Identifier used to match the furniture definition.[/*]
[*][b]ReservedColor[/b]
The color used for the display area. Defaults to #FF00FF.[/*]
[*][b]SpecifiedImage[/b]
A custom image path that can be selected through [b]Specified Image[/b] in the furniture settings.[/*]
[*][b]RenderLightGlows[/b]
Whether the furniture's glow effects should be rendered.[/*]
[*][b]ViewSettings.OffsetX[/b]
Default horizontal offset.[/*]
[*][b]ViewSettings.OffsetY[/b]
Default vertical offset.[/*]
[*][b]ViewSettings.Zoom[/b]
Default zoom.[/*]
[*][b]ViewSettings.ParallaxStrength[/b]
Default parallax strength.[/*]
[*][b]AllowRightClickConfig[/b]
Whether right-click configuration is allowed for that furniture.[/*]
[/list][center][/center]

[size=5][b]Current Support Scope[/b][/size]

[size=5][b]Registering Images from Mods[/b][/size]

TrueWindow 1.0.6 or later provides an API for adding images to the furniture display source options.

Add TrueWindow to your manifest dependencies:

[code]
"Dependencies": [
  {
    "UniqueID": "kaniclub.TrueWindow",
    "MinimumVersion": "1.0.6",
    "IsRequired": true
  }
][/code]
Define the API interface in your mod:

[code]
public interface ITrueWindowApi
{
    void RegisterImageSource(
        string modId,
        string imageId,
        string displayName,
        string filePath
    );
}[/code]
Retrieve the API and register your images during the GameLaunched event. For example:

[code]
public override void Entry(IModHelper helper)
{
    helper.Events.GameLoop.GameLaunched += (_, _) =>
    {
        var api = helper.ModRegistry.GetApi<ITrueWindowApi>(
            "kaniclub.TrueWindow"
        );

        api?.RegisterImageSource(
            ModManifest.UniqueID,
            "my_view",
            "My Custom View",
            System.IO.Path.Combine(
                helper.DirectoryPath, "images", "my_view.png"
            )
        );
    };
}[/code]
[list]
[*][b]modId[/b]: Your mod's UniqueID.[/*]
[*][b]imageId[/b]: A unique, stable ID within your mod. Do not include the installation directory; this ID is used to preserve saved selections.[/*]
[*][b]displayName[/b]: The name shown in the display source options.[/*]
[*][b]filePath[/b]: The absolute path to a PNG, JPG, or JPEG image.[/*]
[/list]
Call RegisterImageSource once for each image. Registering the same modId and imageId again replaces the existing entry.

Registered images are available to all TrueWindow-enabled furniture. Image data is loaded when selected, and display settings are shared within the same location.

Currently supported:

[list]
[*]Furniture: [b]Supported[/b][/*]
[/list]

Not currently supported:

[list]
[*]Buildings[/*]
[*]Wall tiles[/*]
[*]Wallpaper[/*]
[*]Direct map tile replacement[/*]
[/list][center][/center]

[size=5][b]Summary[/b][/size]

TrueWindow is not a mod that adds windows by itself.
It is a mod that provides the [b]window-view functionality[/b] for compatible furniture.

If you want to add new windows, use TrueWindow together with a Content Patcher pack or another mod that adds [b]TrueWindow-enabled furniture[/b].
